description: A polling place lead needs to confirm that each worker packet includes the right materials, credentials, emergency contacts, opening procedures, and quick-reference instructions before the day begins. All election offices and locations are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 44-year-old site lead responsible for opening a polling location smoothly
user_profile.context: The site has enough materials overall, but not enough confidence that each worker packet is complete and correctly assembled
user_profile.communication_style: Orderly and procedural, wants completeness checked by role rather than by memory

fact_sheet.fact: Each Poll Worker Packet must contain one 'Form CW-04: Packet Contents Checklist', dated October 15, 2024.
Each worker's laminated ID badge must display a unique 6-digit Worker ID number and their assigned role.
The primary contact for ballot shortages or material discrepancies is Deputy Clerk Maria Garcia at the Aethelburg County Elections Office, phone number 555-0123.
The 'Zero Report' tape, confirming zero votes have been cast, must be printed from each Pro-Vote 3000 machine at 6:15 AM.
The Site Lead packet contains the master key, labeled 'NCC-MASTER-01', for the main ballot storage closet (Room 104B).
Each Ballot Judge packet must include a logbook titled 'Form BJ-11: Tamper-Evident Seal Log'.
The Check-in Clerk packets must each contain a password card for the 'PollPad' electronic check-in system; the password for November 5, 2024 is 'NorthwoodVote!24'.
The Greeter role packet must include one (1) blue 'Voter Assistance' vest, size Large.
The Northwood Community Center polling location is assigned five (5) Pro-Vote 3000 voting machines for this election.
For technical support with the Pro-Vote 3000 machines or PollPad tablets, call the Aethelburg County IT Help Desk at 555-0182.
All poll workers are required to sign the 'Oath of Office' (Form PW-01) before handling any official election materials, no later than 6:00 AM.
Every worker packet must contain a laminated 4x6 inch 'Quick Reference Guide' (QRG-2024) outlining common voter issues.
The Site Lead's ID badge has a red border for easy identification by workers and election officials.
In case of a medical emergency, first call 911, then immediately notify the Central Command office at 555-0100.
The Site Lead must verify the serial numbers on all five Pro-Vote 3000 machines against the 'Form OP-01: Equipment Inventory' by 5:30 AM.
The asset tag for the single ADA-compliant voting machine at the Northwood location is PV3K-AET-8805.
Each worker packet includes one voucher for a complimentary beverage from the 'Corner Perk Cafe' located next to the polling place.
To report a media inquiry or press presence, contact the County Communications Director, Liam Smith, at 555-0112 before providing any statements.
The Check-in Clerk packet contains the official hard-copy voter roll in a red binder as a backup for the electronic system.
The American flag must be displayed outside the main entrance of the Northwood Community Center by 6:45 AM as per Aethelburg County Election Code 113.4.
To access the county's end-of-day reporting portal, the Site Lead must use the URL https://reports.aethelburg.gov/electionday and their assigned 8-digit PIN.
Each of the three main supply bins (labeled BIN-GEN-01 through BIN-GEN-03) should contain 500 'I Voted' stickers of the 'Aethelburg Oak Tree' design.
Each Ballot Judge packet contains a set of two unique, paired keys (labeled VMAK-1A and VMAK-1B) required to activate a Pro-Vote 3000 machine.
The non-emergency security contact for the Northwood Community Center is building manager Frank Miller, reachable at 555-0199.
The signed 'Zero Report' tapes from all five machines must be posted on the 'Official Notices' board by 6:55 AM for public viewing.
Each packet must contain two black ink pens from the brand 'PenCo' and one pre-sharpened No. 2 pencil.
